clue.text: Quail when one's left imprisoned by magistrates

indicators.note: being imprisoned by something means being shut up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the magistrates sitting in court are collectively the bench

explanation.surface: Someone flinches at the thought of being locked up by the local magistrates.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to flinch or shrink back in fear, which is the old sense of the verb.

clue.text: Inspection requiring a double take?

parts.note: a quick inspection named by two words for viewing, as if one had to take a glance twice

explanation.definitionFit: A look-see is informal for a quick look or inspection, a glance at something.

clue.text: Extremely close attention needed to furnish home

indicators.note: furnishing a home puts things inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a nest is a home, especially a bird's
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Close attention to detail is required when furnishing a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of near means closest of all, at the least distance.

clue.text: Controller used in shock treatment

parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair, and a small pin keeps it under control

explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped wire pin holds a woman's hair in place.

clue.text: Went before parking gets withdrawn

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
receded means drew back or withdrew

explanation.surface: Someone left ahead of the others once their parking permit was cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that preceded came earlier in time or order, i.e. it went first.

clue.text: Spectacular moonrises seen in space

indicators.note: a spectacular display jumbles the letters into a striking new order

explanation.surface: A dramatic rising of the moon is visible in outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: Roominess means spaciousness, plenty of room.

clue.text: Queen's palace torn almost completely asunder

indicators.note: torn asunder means ripped apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged
almost completely means all but the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A royal palace has been nearly ripped to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost completely' trims TORN to TOR; 'asunder' rearranges PALACE and TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last queen of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Line up on quarterdeck in formal wear

parts.note: to dress ranks is the military order to line up
a quarter of a deck of cards is one suit

explanation.surface: Sailors form up in line on a ship's quarterdeck in full uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarterdeck' is part of a ship in the surface, but read as a quarter of a deck of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress suit is a man's evening suit for formal occasions.

clue.text: Cause of outburst as school duty list is put up after daybreak

indicators.note: the school and duty list pieces come after the daybreak one

parts.note: the break, or start, of day is its first letter
Eton is the English public school

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up writes it from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties in turn

explanation.surface: A school's duty roster is posted at dawn and provokes an angry outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is put up' reverses ROTA to give ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator sets off an explosive charge, the cause of a blast.

clue.text: Several open spaces for a meeting

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some public squares are being chosen as venues for a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' is a link: the two words simply meet, side by side. The plural of the Latin forum is used in English for public squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman public squares were each a forum, and the Latin plural names several of them.

clue.text: Rambling with company in natural surroundings

indicators.note: a natural word placed as surroundings for company encloses it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: inherent means natural, built into the thing itself

explanation.surface: Someone walks in the countryside in company, enjoying the natural scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' pretends to be a country walk, but it means speech that wanders without sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambling talk lacks clear logic and connection, the hallmark of muddled, disjointed speech.

clue.text: Dormant reptile has secured shelter

indicators.note: a container that has secured something holds it fast inside

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake, a reptile
lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A sleepy snake has found itself a sheltered spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant is inactive as though sleeping, the literal state of slumber.

clue.text: Stop withdrawal of assistance to parent and child

indicators.note: a withdrawal pulls the word back, so the word for assistance is read in retreat, right to left

parts.note: aid means assistance
pa is an informal word for a father, a parent
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A family's benefit payment to a father and his son is halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a verb but is a noun: an organ stop, a set of pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: An open or stopped diapason is a principal organ stop, the foundation rank of pipes.

clue.text: Approach taken by exercise books to magical figure

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible
an angle is a way of approaching a problem

explanation.surface: A method gets copied into school exercise books for drawing a wizard's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pointed star drawn in one stroke is used in magic and occult ritual.

clue.text: New court in summary sitting designated areas for police action

indicators.note: one piece goes in another

parts.note: a precis is a summary

explanation.surface: A new court sits in summary session to rule on where the police operate.
explanation.definitionFit: Police precincts are the districts each station is responsible for.

clue.text: A disturbance in vision after dark

definitions.text: A disturbance in vision after dark

parts.words: A disturbance in vision after dark
parts.note: a frightening dream troubles what one sees in sleep at night, not an eye complaint

explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream is a disturbing vision experienced during the night's sleep.

clue.text: Highly informative device

parts.note: an instrument that tells you how high up you are, informing you about height

explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft instrument measures and shows altitude.

clue.text: Messenger's instruction to place stake on small number at the outset

parts.note: go is an instruction to proceed
to bet is to place a stake
wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: the outset of a word is its beginning, so only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A runner is told to put money on a low number from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermediary carries messages between two parties.

clue.text: Mock Turtle's introduction to relation

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening, so only the first letter of the turtle is used

parts.note: an aunt is a relation

explanation.surface: The Mock Turtle from Alice in Wonderland is being introduced to a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock Turtle' reads as the Alice character, but 'Mock' is the verb to define.
explanation.definitionFit: To taunt someone is to jeer at and ridicule them.

clue.text: Rowers reducing power at the start

indicators.note: reducing a word cuts it down, so a letter is taken away
places the removal at the opening of the word for power

parts.note: weight means power or influence, as in carrying weight

explanation.surface: A rowing crew is easing off its effort at the start of the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing crew of that number of oarsmen is named by the number itself.

clue.text: Splash in curative waters to improve all round

indicators.note: one piece placed all round another encloses it

parts.note: to better something is to improve it
a spa is a spring of healing mineral waters

explanation.surface: Bathing in healing spa waters will make you feel better all over.
explanation.definitionFit: To bespatter is to splash with drops of liquid or mud.

clue.text: Stick with sailors in this part of bay

parts.note: paste is a glue that sticks things
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: A glue is used by sailors in a part of a coastal bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' is not a coastal inlet but a bay horse, reddish-brown with a black mane.
explanation.definitionFit: The pastern is the part of a horse's leg between fetlock and hoof.

clue.text: Stout container in reservoir on a road

parts.note: a tank is a reservoir for holding liquid

explanation.surface: A sturdy vessel sits in a reservoir beside a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like an adjective for sturdy, but it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large beer mug for drinking ale or stout.

clue.text: Angry after survey shows unpleasant prospect

indicators.note: the angry piece comes after the survey one

parts.note: to eye something is to survey it
sore is informal for angry

explanation.surface: A surveyor is cross after the inspection reveals an ugly view.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ugly that spoils the view is a blot on the landscape.

clue.text: Convey thanks, turning in eventually

indicators.note: one piece goes in another

parts.note: in time means eventually

indicators.note: turning the word for thanks turns it round, right to left

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone eventually gets round to passing on their thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the British slang for thanks; 'Convey' means hint at, not carry.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to make known or communicate indirectly, to hint.

clue.text: Verse Tennyson composed leaving central New York

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged
the New York letters are taken from the middle of the poet's name, so they leave its centre

explanation.surface: The poet Tennyson wrote a poem after moving out of the middle of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing NY from the middle of TENNYSON leaves TENSON; 'composed' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a fourteen-line poem, a form of verse.

clue.text: Time to take further exercise after daily drink

indicators.note: the time and exercise pieces come after the daily one

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British cleaning lady who comes in every day
to reuse something is to exercise or use it again

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to get back to the gym after their daily drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like an adjective for the drink but is a noun: a char, a daily cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a green or yellow herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks.

clue.text: Soon to become a prolific writer, apparently!

definitions.meaning: an old word meaning shortly or presently
anonymous author credits are so common that the abbreviation seems to be one very busy writer

explanation.surface: Someone expects shortly to turn into a highly productive author.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is archaic for presently, and the abbreviation of anonymous credits countless unsigned works.

clue.text: Cutting short action in second trial

parts.note: a hearing is a trial of a case in court

explanation.surface: A judge curtails a lawsuit during a retrial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' and 'trial' suggest a legal case; the definition is clipping, as of sheep's wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearing clips fleece or hair close, an act of cutting it down short.

clue.text: Failed to attend as agreed

definitions.meaning: nodding off means dozing, so paying no attention
showed assent by bobbing the head

explanation.surface: Someone skipped the meeting, as everybody had agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: One nods off when not attending, and nods the head in assent.
